Definition: from ληΐζομαι (to plunder); a brigand:--robber, thief.
BiblicalUsage: lēistḗs means robber, thief, and the word keeps turning up at decisive moments. In Luke 10:30, "and fell among thieves"; and in John 10:1, "the same is a thief and a robber.". In John 18:40, "Now Barabbas was a robber."; and in 2 Corinthians 11:26, "[in] perils of robbers".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the robber is the test of every heart — the thieves on the Jericho road strip and wound, and the crowd chose Barabbas the robber over Christ. I hold that Jesus is the door the robber refuses and the neighbour the wounded man needs. My position is that I will not climb in some other way; I will enter by the door.
